newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-DORTMUND WEATHER UNITED STORM TO REACH FINAL.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DORTMUND WEATHER UNITED STORM TO REACH FINAL.

text.p: An eighth minute goal by midfielder Lars Ricken gave Borussia Dortmund a 1-0 win over Manchester United at Old Trafford on Wednesday and a place in the European Cup final against holders Juventus on May 28.
Dortmund won the semifinal 2-0 on aggregate to become the first German side to reach the final since Bayern Munich 10 years ago.

The German team, marshalled by Juergen Kohler and Wolfgang Feiersinger, defended superbly and weathered almost non-stop United attacks as they deservedly qualified for the final in Munich's Olympic Stadium.
Dortmund stunned the majority of the 53,000-plus capacity crowd when they took the early lead in the second leg, meaning United had to score three times to win.

From a throw-in on the right, Andreas Moeller fed the ball to Ricken, who turned and sped past Gary Pallister before firing into the far corner past goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel, who reacted too slowly to divert the ball to safety.

United had more than a dozen clear-cut scoring chances but it was never going to be their night after Eric Cantona, Andy Cole and especially Pallister all wasted excellent opportunities before halftime.
